issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) in SealSaloon, but the solution's SealSaloon class implements a method named computeMealCost(Meal). Additionally, solution Main invokes calculateTotalPrice(...) while SealSaloon only defines computeMealCost(...). The template Main uses computeMealCost(...) as well. This inconsistent naming across problem, template, and solution will confuse students about the expected method name and causes mismatches that can lead to compilation errors or unclear mapping of requirements to code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename computeMealCost(...) in SealSaloon to calculateTotalPrice(...) (or vice versa) and update all references in Main and the problem statement so they match. Ensure the method signature (static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal)) matches the problem specification and that corresponding comments/examples in Main use the same name.
